title: Malaysia Oil Palm Precision Agriculture
thesis: A fictional Malaysian oil palm grower runs block agronomy on Snowflake: curated dynamic tables turn daily block observations into ripeness, crop-loss, fertilizer and sensor KPIs, Snowflake ML ranks next-week crop-loss risk, and Cortex answers questions with SQL and SOP citations.

talking_points: Thirty synthetic blocks on estates near Kluang, Kuantan, Sandakan and Bintulu, with one set of KPIs: ripe bunch rate, crop-loss events, fertilizer intensity and tonnes of FFB harvested.
Each KPI is computed as an explicit numerator and denominator in a dynamic table, so any figure drills back to block-day rows. The thresholds are demo settings, not agronomic guidance.
The cause chart ranks crop-loss causes by the unripe bunches they leave behind.
tabs.call_out: Plantation KPIs the whole group can trace to source

transition.line: Where is the next crop-loss event most likely?

talking_points: A Snowflake ML classification model estimates, per block, the chance of a crop-loss event within 7 days.
Its holdout line reports precision and recall on the latest labelled days next to the base rate, so the audience sees how good it really is.
Anomaly detection picks out unusual soil moisture deficit days, and a forecast projects the grower's daily FFB harvest 14 days ahead.
tabs.call_out: Measured ML that runs where the data lives

transition.line: Can we trust the field data behind these scores?

talking_points: Sensor uptime and mapped hectares show how much of each estate is actually observed.
Plotting scouting completion against ripe bunch rate per block shows where the two move together; treat it as a correlation, not a cause.
The action memo proposes three prioritised actions, drawn only from the KPI, crop-loss, cause and risk tables.
show: Scouting completion vs ripe bunch rate
tabs.call_out: Draft actions grounded in data, approved by people

transition.line: What if a field sensor alarms during the meeting?

talking_points: Soil moisture deficit and drain water level readings arrive in RAW.LIVE_TELEMETRY, either from the built-in simulator or from AWS IoT Core via S3 and Snowpipe.
A Snowflake alert records each ALARM reading with an SOP hint and the block's risk band, and emails the agronomist on duty.
tabs.call_out: Sensor alarm to agronomist email on one platform

transition.line: Let's ask the data in plain language.

talking_points: The Cortex Agent combines Cortex Analyst on the semantic view for numbers with Cortex Search on synthetic crop-loss SOPs for procedures.
Every answer displays the SQL it ran and the SOP IDs it cited.
tabs.call_out: Answers you can check line by line

transition.line: And this is the build behind it.

talking_points: One shared core supports two builds: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake with IoT Core, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q.
All data is synthetic and regenerated identically from the repository.
tabs.call_out: A governed Snowflake core with an optional AWS edge
